title: Microsoft Intune: Administrator protection settings in the settings catalog and account protection template
summary: Hold: the automation column presents policy creation as configuring Administrator protection, but the referenced operation only creates the policy container. The assurance that devices without the Intune policy keep their current elevation behaviour also overlooks Microsoft's documented automatic enablement for Windows security baseline users.

claims.claim: The cited Account protection policy page does not list Administrator protection settings in the template.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune Adminless Administrator protection account protection template settings. Read Account protection policy for endpoint security in Intune in full and search excerpts for ref-account-protection-settings; neither lists Administrator protection in that template.

claims.claim: The printed Intune admin centre route reaches Add settings for a Windows settings catalog policy.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. ... Windows 10 and later ... Profile type: Select Settings catalog. ... In Configuration settings, select Add settings.
claims.fix: Use 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog > Create > Basics > Configuration settings > Add settings > Local Policies Security Options > User Account Control Type Of Admin Approval Mode'. The final category and setting are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/. Retain the other prompt-setting name in the note.

claims.claim: Creating a settings catalog policy requires at least the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies is the automation equivalent for enabling Administrator protection and choosing its elevation prompt.
claims.quote: Create a new deviceManagementConfigurationPolicy object. ... name | String | Policy name ... settingCount | Int32 | Number of settings
claims.fix: Narrow controls[0].governs to 'Creation of a settings catalog policy; Administrator protection settings are configured separately'. Retain the valid POST /beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies call, but change the note to 'Graph creates the policy container only; it does not enable Administrator protection or set its elevation prompt. In the UI, configure Local Policies Security Options using the two settings named in What's changing. Needs at least Policy and Profile Manager.' The setting-creation reference is https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/intune-deviceconfigv2-devicemanagementconfigurationsetting-create?view=graph-rest-beta, but it does not identify these feature-specific settings, so do not substitute an inferred feature-specific call.
